/speckit-specify This repository already contains `logredact`, a command-line tool that removes personal data from log files. Read the existing code and any documentation in the repository before changing it. Change it as follows; everything else it does now must keep working exactly as it does.

1. **Phone numbers.** Phone numbers in international format, a `+` followed by 8 to 15 digits such as `+14155552671`, become `[PHONE]`. With `--count`, the summary on standard error becomes `emails=N ips=N cards=N phones=N`.

2. **Output folder.** A new option `--out-dir DIR` writes the redacted lines of each FILE to a file with the same name in DIR (the file's name only, without its directories) instead of to standard output. DIR is created, with any missing parent directories, if it does not exist, and an existing file of that name in DIR is replaced. When every FILE has been processed, the tool prints `wrote N files` to standard output, where N is the number of output files written. A FILE that cannot be read is handled as it is now: an error message naming the file on standard error, and exit status 2.

Examples, for files `app.log` (containing `user jane@example.com`) and `web.log` (containing `GET / from 10.0.0.7`):

```
$ printf 'call +14155552671 now\n' | python -m logredact
call [PHONE] now

$ printf 'a@b.io +442071838750\n' | python -m logredact --count
[EMAIL] [PHONE]
emails=1 ips=0 cards=0 phones=1        <- on standard error

$ python -m logredact --out-dir clean app.log web.log
wrote 2 files
```

### What I read first

`src/logredact/{cli,redact}.py`, the feature-001 spec and CLI contract, the constitution, and the existing test suite. The spec is written as an **amendment**: requirement IDs are local (`FR-001`…`FR-023`), and existing behaviour is referenced as `001:FR-025` so the two documents can't be confused. `FR-023` requires everything not amended to be preserved.

### Decisions I made rather than asking (all recorded in Assumptions with rationale)

- **`--out-dir` with no FILE** → usage diagnostic, exit 2. Standard input has no name to derive an output file from; silently writing to stdout would ignore a typed option (the thing `001:FR-029` forbids) and `wrote 0 files` would discard output silently (Principle II).
- **Output path identical to its own input** (`--out-dir .` on `app.log`) → refused with a diagnostic, exit 2, file untouched. Replacing it would truncate the input mid-read and leave a damaged file that looks like a successful redaction.
- **`N` counts FILE arguments**, not distinct destination paths, so two inputs sharing a name report `wrote 2 files`. **`wrote 1 files`** is not pluralized — the request gave the literal form.
- **`+` with 16+ digits** → no match at all, no partial redaction (mirrors `001:FR-016`/`001:FR-012`).
- **Phone is last in the same-position tie-break**, leaving `001:FR-019` literally unchanged; the only possible tie is with an email, so `+15551234567@example.com` stays `[EMAIL]`.

### One behaviour change worth your attention

Adding phone matching changes the output of exactly one existing input shape beyond adding `[PHONE]`: a `+` immediately followed by a **Luhn-valid 13-to-15-digit run**. I verified against the current tool that `+4111111111119` yields `+[CARD]` / `cards=1` today; under the new rule the leftmost-match rule makes it `[PHONE]` / `phones=1`. This follows directly from the phone rule you specified, so I spec'd it that way and flagged it in Edge Cases and Assumptions rather than carving out an exception.

I also checked the test suite: no existing test asserts on `+`-prefixed digit runs, so the only existing assertions this feature invalidates are the `emails=N ips=N cards=N` summary strings (SC-004).
